# Functions of qiime2R

read_qza() - Function for reading artifacts (.qza).

qza_to_phyloseq() - Imports multiple artifacts to produce a phyloseq object.

read_q2metadata() - Reads qiime2 metadata file (containing q2-types definition line).

write_q2manifest() - Writes a read manifest file to import data into qiime2.

theme_q2r() - A ggplot2 theme for publication-type figures.

print_provenance() - A function to display provenance information.

is_q2metadata() - A function to check if a file is a qiime2 metadata file.

parse_taxonomy() - A function to parse taxonomy strings and return a table where each column is a taxonomic class.

parse_ordination() - A function to parse the internal ordination format.

# Nomenclature

The manuscript and code files may utilize different naming conventions for groups and treatments as follows:

**Manuscript Name**  | **Related Script Name(s)**
------------- | -------------
Sample Type  | Type
Microbial Depletion  | Depletion, Dep, or Treatment
Microbial Density  | Concentration, Con, PW_Percentage, or Percentage
Pond Source | Pond, or Pond_Treatment

# Description of Test

To test for a monotonic (a function between ordered sets that preserves the given order) trend (correlation) across ordered groups (i.e., ordinal IV), this code will use a Jonckheere-Terpstra Test. Your dependent variable must be continuous or ordinal, and you must expect increasing or decreasing trends (not just any difference).

The exact calculation requires that there be no ties and that the sample size is less than 100.

When data are tied and sample size is at most 100 permutation p-value is returned. Recommend that the user set nperm to be 1000 or higher if permutation p-value is desired.

## Gut Samples {.tabset .tabset-pills}

### PLE

```{r Gut_PLE, warning=FALSE}
metadata<-read_q2metadata("/core-metrics-results-gut/Tadpole_Metadata_Gut_Alpha_Con_Q2.txt")

metadata_PLE <- metadata[ which(metadata$Pond == "PLE"), ]

#### Formula of the form lhs ~ rhs where lhs gives the data values and rhs the corresponding groups.

#### ASVs
JonckheereTerpstraTest(ASVs ~ Percentage, metadata_PLE, nperm = 5000)

#### Shannon
JonckheereTerpstraTest(Shannon ~ Percentage, metadata_PLE, nperm = 5000)

#### Faiths
JonckheereTerpstraTest(Faith ~ Percentage, metadata_PLE, nperm = 5000)

#### Evenness
JonckheereTerpstraTest(Evenness ~ Percentage, metadata_PLE, nperm = 5000)
```

### PM
